message.content:
Fix several web-security findings from an audit in the Nxeon platform. Work EXCLUSIVELY in /opt/nxeon-wt-fix-web (branch hardening/web-ssrf-xss). node_modules symlinked. Do NOT run build/prisma commands — code only.

FINDING 1 (MED — fix first): DNS-rebinding (TOCTOU) SSRF in the agency site scraper. lib/agency/scrape.ts: `assertHostPublic()` (~177-203) resolves the hostname and checks the IPs are public, but `scrapeSite()` (~476) then calls `fetch(url)` with the HOSTNAME, which undici re-resolves on connect — a 0-TTL DNS record that answers public on the check and 169.254.169.254 / 127.0.0.1 / 10.x on connect slips through, reaching cloud metadata / the Proxmox API (127.0.0.1:8006) / internal services, with the bytes flowing into demo generation (exfil). The codebase ALREADY has the correct fix pattern: app/api/tools/http-headers/route.ts uses a `pinnedAgent()` (custom undici Agent whose `connect.lookup` dials the pre-vetted IP). FIX: make scrapeSite resolve once (reuse the vetted IP from assertHostPublic) and fetch via a pinned undici Agent that connects to that exact IP while preserving the Host header + TLS SNI. Re-validate every redirect hop's IP the same way (resolve+check+pin) — don't blindly follow redirects to a new host. Copy/adapt pinnedAgent from the http-headers tool.

FINDING 2 (LOW): stored XSS via SVG on board attachments. app/api/board/attachments/route.ts accepts any MIME and maps image/svg+xml to IMAGE; app/api/board/attachments/[id]/route.ts serves the client-declared att.mime with Content-Disposition: inline and NO X-Content-Type-Options and NO CSP — an admin-uploaded scripted SVG runs JS in the admin origin. FIX (mirror app/api/chat/attachment/[id]/route.ts + app/api/mail/signature-image/[id]/route.ts which do this right): on the board attachment SERVE route add headers `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox`; and on the UPLOAD route reject/normalize image/svg+xml — allow-list real raster image MIMEs (validate by byte signature if the other routes do, e.g. isAllowedImageMime), so a scripted SVG can't be stored+served as an image.

FINDING 3 (LOW): session cookie Secure flag is gated behind an extra env var while the impersonation cookie isn't. lib/auth.ts:27 sets the session + nxeon_authed cookie `secure = NODE_ENV==="production" && process.env.COOKIE_SECURE==="1"`, but lib/auth.ts:194 sets the impersonation cookie `secure = NODE_ENV==="production"`. FIX: make the session/nxeon_authed cookie's `secure` gate on `NODE_ENV==="production"` alone (matching the impersonation cookie), so a deploy that forgets COOKIE_SECURE=1 can't ship a non-Secure session cookie. (Prod currently sets COOKIE_SECURE=1, so this is a safe hardening of the default — verify you don't break local http dev, which is NODE_ENV!=="production" so stays non-secure.)

FINDING 4 (LOW/optional): app/api/tools/dns/route.ts (~190-210) only blocks the literal "localhost" and can return internal A/AAAA records if the resolver knows internal names. Optional: strip private/reserved (RFC1918, 127/8, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7, etc.) addresses from the returned records so the public tool can't enumerate internal names. Reuse any existing net-guard classifier (lib/tools/net-guard.ts) if suitable.

DELIVER end-to-end, then commit `git add -A && git commit -m "fix(web): pin scraper fetch to vetted IP (SSRF rebind); nosniff+CSP+SVG-reject on board attachments; harden session-cookie Secure default; DNS tool internal-record filter"` (trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>), `git push -u origin hardening/web-ssrf-xss`. REPORT (factual): each fix, files changed, and confirm the scraper now connects only to the vetted IP (incl. redirects). Don't claim tested.

I'm ready to implement the SSRF rebind fix for scrape.ts. I need to import undici's Agent and fetch utilities along with the net module, create a helper to pin the agent to a specific address, and then refactor the scrape function so that address validation returns the actual addresses which get used for a pinned connection, with re-validation on each redirect. I'll manage agent lifecycle by closing the previous one before each redirect and closing the final agent in the outer finally block that already handles the timeout cleanup. Writing fetch options...

I'm noticing a type mismatch here—undici's Response type doesn't align with the global Response type that the rest of the code expects, particularly around methods like `res.body.getReader()`. The annotation `let res: Response` assumes the global type, but `undiciFetch` returns undici's own Response, which could cause TypeScript errors downstream.

The simplest fix would be to import and alias undici's Response type, then use that consistently throughout the function, or cast the result explicitly. Since the structures are largely compatible, the real issue is just getting TypeScript to recognize them as the same type. I could cast the result as `unknown` then to the global `Response` type to sidestep the typing issues entirely. Since undici's Response implements all the methods I'm actually using—`.status`, `.headers.get()`, `.ok`, `.body.getReader()`, `.text()`—the cast is safe at runtime and keeps the rest of the code unchanged.

I'll go with the cast approach. Then I need to add cleanup in the finally block to close the agent and clear the timeout. The redirect logic already handles re-validation and re-pinning for new hosts, and IPv6 addresses are properly detected via the `isIP` check returning 6. Now I'm ready to write the edits for scrape.ts, but I'm also noticing a second issue around board attachments in the upload route.

The problem is SVG files — they come in as `image/svg+xml` which gets marked as kind IMAGE and served inline, creating a security risk. I need to reject SVGs or normalize them, allowing only real raster image MIME types. I can use the existing `isAllowedImageMime` validation from chat-attachment to enforce an allow-list, similar to how other routes validate by byte signature. For files and videos it's fine since they're served as downloads, but images need stricter handling. I should restructure the upload flow to read the buffer once upfront, then validate it if it's an image before writing to disk. For images, I'll use the byte validation to get the canonical mime type and reject anything that doesn't pass (including SVG). For non-images like video, I can skip the buffer validation since I only need it for image security checks, though writeFile will still read the arrayBuffer anyway.

Now I'm importing the image validation utilities and realizing validateImageBytes enforces a 5MB cap, but board images should allow up to 50MB...

so I need to use sniffImageMime and isAllowedImageMime directly without that stricter validation. I'll read the buffer, check if it's an image, sniff the actual MIME type, reject SVG and disallowed formats, then store the sniffed MIME.

Let me trace through the edge cases: SVG with image/svg+xml gets sniffed as null and rejected—good. A legit image where the client sends a generic MIME like application/octet-stream gets classified as FILE and served as a download with the nosniff header, so the browser won't try to render it as an image—safe. An SVG disguised as text/plain or application/octet-stream also gets treated as a FILE download, protected by nosniff—also safe.

For the stored MIME, I'm setting it to the sniffed value for images, so the serve route uses a safe raster MIME. The size cap is computed based on kind before reading the buffer, and the order stays: compute MIME and kind, check the cap against file.size, read the buffer, validate the image, then write. I'll replace the redundant `Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer())` call in the write with the buffer I've already read.

On the serve route, I need to add security headers—X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and a CSP with default-src 'none' and sandbox. These should apply to all response kinds for defense in depth, though I'm still thinking through whether sandbox CSP on video responses would cause issues. both 200 and 206 responses. I'm adding security headers to the base headers object so they apply consistently: setting nosniff to prevent MIME type sniffing, and a CSP with sandbox mode to restrict what inline content can do. This should protect against SVG-based attacks, though I'm realizing existing SVG attachments stored in the database would still be served with their original MIME type and might not be properly sandboxed by the browser.

Now I'm looking at the cookie security setting in auth.ts — I can simplify the secure flag to just check if we're in production, removing the redundant environment variable check. That applies to both session and nxeon_authed cookies.

For the DNS route, I need to filter out private and reserved IP addresses from the A and AAAA records being returned, reusing the isBlockedIp utility that's already available.…

content.text:
All four findings fixed, committed, and pushed to `origin/hardening/web-ssrf-xss`. Report follows.

## Summary

**Finding 1 (MED) — DNS-rebinding SSRF in the site scraper** — `/opt/nxeon-wt-fix-web/lib/agency/scrape.ts`
- Added undici imports (`Agent`, `fetch as undiciFetch`, `Response` type) — using undici's own fetch so a custom dispatcher is accepted (same constraint the http-headers tool documents).
- Added a `pinnedAgent(address)` helper adapted from `app/api/tools/http-headers/route.ts`: a custom undici `Agent` whose `connect.lookup` returns the pre-vetted IP (answering both the `{all:true}` array form and the positional callback form), so the hostname is never re-resolved on connect. Host header + TLS SNI still come from the URL.
- Rewrote `scrapeSite`'s fetch loop: `assertHostPublic()` already returns the resolved addresses, so each hop now captures those addresses, builds a `pinnedAgent(vettedAddrs[0])`, and fetches via `undiciFetch(..., { dispatcher: agent })`. `readCapped` retyped to the undici `Response`.
- Redirects: unchanged manual-redirect logic still runs `assertHostPublic` at the top of every iteration, and a new pinned agent is built for the new host each hop — so every redirect hop is resolve+check+pin, never blindly followed.
- Lifecycle: one `Agent` per hop, closed before the next hop is pinned and again in the outer `finally` (so return-inside-loop paths don't leak sockets).
- Net effect: the scraper connects only to the exact IP that passed `assertHostPublic`, on the initial URL and on every redirect hop; the 0-TTL rebind to `169.254.169.254` / `127.0.0.1:8006` / `10.x` no longer works.

**Finding 2 (LOW) — stored XSS via SVG on board attachments**
- Serve route `app/api/board/attachments/[id]/route.ts`: added `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` to `baseHeaders` (covers both the 200 and 206/Range responses), matching the chat/mail image routes. This also neuters any legacy SVG already stored.
- Upload route `app/api/board/attachments/route.ts`: for anything mapped to `IMAGE`, the bytes are now read once and validated with `sniffImageMime` + `isAllowedImageMime` (from `lib/chat-attachment.ts`); `image/svg+xml`, spoofed, or non-raster images are rejected 400, and the stored MIME is set to the sniffed canonical raster type. Non-image MIMEs fall through as FILE/VIDEO (served with a download disposition), unchanged.

**Finding 3 (LOW) — session cookie Secure default** — `/opt/nxeon-wt-fix-web/lib/auth.ts:27`
- Changed the session + `nxeon_authed` cookie `secure` gate from `NODE_ENV==="production" && COOKIE_SECURE==="1"` to `NODE_ENV==="production"` alone, matching the impersonation cookie. Local http dev (NODE_ENV !== "production") stays non-secure.

**Finding 4 (LOW) — DNS tool leaking internal records** — `/opt/nxeon-wt-fix-web/app/api/tools/dns/route.ts`
- Imported `isBlockedIp` from `lib/tools/net-guard.ts` and filtered private/reserved addresses out of the returned A and AAAA record sets.

Committed as `fix(web): pin scraper fetch to vetted IP (SSRF rebind); nosniff+CSP+SVG-reject on board attachments; harden session-cookie Secure default; DNS tool internal-record filter` and pushed with upstream tracking. Per instructions I did not run build/prisma/tsc, so this is not test-verified.
